Given $\frac{\partial Q}{\partial x}-\frac{\partial P}{\partial y}=2 x^{2} + 2 y^{2}$, calculate $\oint_{\partial D}P\,\mathrm dx+Q\,\mathrm dy$ over the positively oriented annular region shown above." :question/worked-solution "Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D,$ then Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Green's theorem can be extended to include regions containing holes. In such cases, we can apply Green's theorem in the same way as before.

Therefore, applying Green's theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\oint_{\partial D}P\,\mathrm dx+Q\,\mathrm dy & =\iint_D 2 x^{2} + 2 y^{2}\,\mathrm dA.\end{aligned}
$$

The region $D$ can be represented in polar coordinates as 

$$\Delta=\{(r,\theta):1\le r\le 5,0\le\theta\le2\pi\}.$$

Recall that the change of variables formula for polar coordinates gives

$$
{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\text{ }dA={∬}_{Δ}\text{ }f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,r\text{ }drd\theta .
$$

Therefore, our double integral becomes

$$
\begin{aligned}\iint_D 2 x^{2} + 2 y^{2}\,\mathrm dA & =\int_{0}^{2 \pi}\int_{1}^{5}2\left(((r\cos\theta)^2+(r\sin\theta)^2)\cdot r\right)\,\mathrm d r\,\mathrm d \theta\\ & =\int_{0}^{2 \pi}\int_{1}^{5}2\left(r^{2}(\cos^2\theta+\sin^2\theta)\cdot r\right)\,\mathrm d r\,\mathrm d \theta\\ & =\int_{0}^{2 \pi}\int_{1}^{5}2 r^{3}\,\mathrm d r\,\mathrm d \theta\\ & =\int_{0}^{2 \pi}\,\mathrm d \theta\cdot \int_{1}^{5}2 r^{3}\,\mathrm d r\\ & =4 \pi\cdot \int_{1}^{5}r^{3}\,\mathrm d r\\ & =4 \pi\cdot \frac{r^{4}}{4}\big|_{1}^{5}\\ & =4 \pi\cdot (\left(\frac{625}{4}\right)-\left(\frac{1}{4}\right))\\ & =2\cdot\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\cdot \left((5)^{4}-\left((1)^{4}\right)\right)\\ & =\pi\cdot \left(625-\left(1\right)\right)\\ & =624 \pi.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["bb276fee-1328-52b2-93a5-0a1d60787d5d"] :db/ensure :question/validate} {:db/id "31a06a5d-40b1-5683-8ce6-dfd63f5d2ab8" :answer/id #uuid "31a06a5d-40b1-5683-8ce6-dfd63f5d2ab8" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "126 \pi" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "11e36d62-94f1-5ba3-af16-1f40060c2cbc" :answer/id #uuid "11e36d62-94f1-5ba3-af16-1f40060c2cbc" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{765 \pi}{2}" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "7e04b873-e352-5358-9d2e-78981f827a83" :answer/id #uuid "7e04b873-e352-5358-9d2e-78981f827a83" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{771 \pi}{2}" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "7602cfab-23bc-5eae-a2c4-1fbd9b5d02de" :answer/id #uuid "7602cfab-23bc-5eae-a2c4-1fbd9b5d02de" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "- \frac{765 \pi}{2}" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "ec38f5f1-a0ed-5b6b-9e09-714a75f8002d" :answer/id #uuid "ec38f5f1-a0ed-5b6b-9e09-714a75f8002d" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "384 \pi" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "900b2dea-1194-5254-b495-708b3b81e6b5" :answer-field/id #uuid "900b2dea-1194-5254-b495-708b3b81e6b5" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/choices ["31a06a5d-40b1-5683-8ce6-dfd63f5d2ab8" "11e36d62-94f1-5ba3-af16-1f40060c2cbc" "7e04b873-e352-5358-9d2e-78981f827a83" "7602cfab-23bc-5eae-a2c4-1fbd9b5d02de" "ec38f5f1-a0ed-5b6b-9e09-714a75f8002d"] :answer-field/correct "11e36d62-94f1-5ba3-af16-1f40060c2cbc" :db/ensure :answer-field/validate} {:db/id "800ffb15-04e7-5a70-992e-e33805e2762f" :question/id #uuid "800ffb15-04e7-5a70-992e-e33805e2762f" :question/problem "![](images/37/37c3ffbceecd99f2c618c1401e392b27620a0e34ce284683446eae4217c5e973.png)

Calculate $\oint_{\partial D}(x^{2} y + y^{3})\,\mathrm dx+(- x^{3} - x y^{2})\,\mathrm dy$, where $D$ is the annular region shown above." :question/worked-solution "Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D,$ then Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Green's theorem can be extended to include regions containing holes. In such cases, we can apply Green's theorem in the same way as before.

We have that $P(x,y)=x^{2} y + y^{3}$ and $Q(x,y)=- x^{3} - x y^{2}.$ So,

For $\partial P/\partial y$ we hold $x$ fixed, and for $\partial Q/\partial x$ we hold $y$ fixed. The component derivatives, including zero contributions, are

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial P}{\partial y} & =\frac{\partial}{\partial y}\left(x^{2} y + y^{3}\right)=\left(3 y^{2}\right)+\left(x^{2}\right)=x^{2} + 3 y^{2}\\ \frac{\partial Q}{\partial x} & =\frac{\partial}{\partial x}\left(- x^{3} - x y^{2}\right)=\left(- 3 x^{2}\right)+\left(- y^{2}\right)=- 3 x^{2} - y^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$\frac{\partial P}{\partial y}=x^{2} + 3 y^{2},\qquad\frac{\partial Q}{\partial x}=- 3 x^{2} - y^{2}.$$

Therefore, applying Green's theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\oint_{\partial D}(x^{2} y + y^{3})\,\mathrm dx+(- x^{3} - x y^{2})\,\mathrm dy & =\iint_D\left(\frac{\partial Q}{\partial x}-\frac{\partial P}{\partial y}\right)\,\mathrm dA\\ & =\iint_D\left(- 3 x^{2} - y^{2}-(x^{2} + 3 y^{2})\right)\,\mathrm dA\\ & =\iint_D(- 4 x^{2} - 4 y^{2})\,\mathrm dA\\ & =\iint_D - 4 \left(x^{2} + y^{2}\right)\,\mathrm dA.\end{aligned}
$$

The region $D$ can be represented in polar coordinates as 

$$\Delta=\{(r,\theta):3\le r\le 4,0\le\theta\le2\pi\}.$$

Recall that the change of variables formula for polar coordinates gives

$$
{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\text{ }dA={∬}_{Δ}\text{ }f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,r\text{ }drd\theta .
$$

Therefore, our double integral becomes

$$
\begin{aligned}\iint_D - 4 \left(x^{2} + y^{2}\right)\,\mathrm dA & =-4\cdot \int_{0}^{2 \pi}\int_{3}^{4}((r\cos\theta)^2+(r\sin\theta)^2)\cdot r\,\mathrm d r\,\mathrm d \theta\\ & =-4\cdot \int_{0}^{2 \pi}\int_{3}^{4}r^{2}(\cos^2\theta+\sin^2\theta)\cdot r\,\mathrm d r\,\mathrm d \theta\\ & =-4\cdot \int_{0}^{2 \pi}\int_{3}^{4}r^{3}\,\mathrm d r\,\mathrm d \theta\\ & =-4\cdot \int_{0}^{2 \pi}\,\mathrm d \theta\cdot \int_{3}^{4}r^{3}\,\mathrm d r\\ & =- 8 \pi\cdot \int_{3}^{4}r^{3}\,\mathrm d r\\ & =- 8 \pi\cdot \frac{r^{4}}{4}\big|_{3}^{4}\\ & =- 8 \pi\cdot (\left(64\right)-\left(\frac{81}{4}\right))\\ & =-1\cdot\left(2 \pi\right)\cdot \left((4)^{4}-\left((3)^{4}\right)\right)\\ & =- 2 \pi\cdot \left(256-\left(81\right)\right)\\ & =- 350 \pi.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["5a78c00f-da46-5e8a-8243-86c98db8401d"] :db/ensure :question/validate} {:db/id "generator" :question-generator/id #uuid "6b09df87-9df8-5588-948a-fb2dc20165c9" :question-generator/script "generate/scratch/17592186133900.py"} [:db/add 17592186133900 :knowledge-point/question-generator "generator"] {:db/id 17592186133900 :knowledge-point/questions ["a54bcbf9-79fa-5632-9386-d8874ad021a4" "800ffb15-04e7-5a70-992e-e33805e2762f" "19907c37-a4a5-570e-a985-43945896ae6b" "5b6c6718-cecd-5d44-9775-b44c08c7c182" "d0e8fd21-3500-5007-9a3c-aa39f399cf8f" "e873ebd8-54e2-5508-997d-3107e1ab89bf"]} [:db/ensure 17592186133900 :knowledge-point/validate]]
